chunks: He said: And Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran narrated to me from Ismail ibn Mansur al-Zubali who said: I heard a man from Azrat who had passed one hundred and twenty years of age say: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying from the pulpit of Kufa: As if I see the son of Hamida who has filled it with justice and equity, just as it had been filled with injustice and oppression. A man stood up to him and asked: Is he from you or from someone else? He said: No, but he is a man from me.

key_terms.ابْنُ حُمَيْدٍ: Son of Hamida (a title for the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'son of Hamida' mentioned by Imam Ali in Kufa?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the early recognition of the Mahdi (a.s.) as a descendant of Ali (a.s.), specifically linking him to the lineage of Hasan or Husayn through the title 'Ibn Hamida'. It serves as a crucial evidence for the Imamate of the Twelfth Imam, countering the Waqifiya who denied his continued existence, and underscores the theological promise of global justice replacing tyranny. The confirmation that he is 'from him' (Ali) emphasizes the direct familial and spiritual connection central to Shia eschatology.
